Ŭl P'aso was the kuksang of Goguryeo under its 9th ruler King Gogukcheon, marking a pivotal moment in the kingdom's history. This position afforded Ŭl P'aso significant influence over the administration and policies of Goguryeo, particularly during times of war and diplomacy.

As the leader of the country, Ŭl P'aso oversaw extensive military campaigns against neighboring tribes and states, expanding Goguryeo's borders and securing its position as a major power in the region. This expansion not only brought immense wealth and resources to the kingdom but also set the stage for future conflicts and strategic alliances.

The legacy of Ŭl P'aso can be seen in the continued influence of Goguryeo on the Korean Peninsula, with many of its cultural achievements and traditions remaining an integral part of modern-day North Korea. Furthermore, Ŭl P'aso's leadership played a significant role in shaping the country's political landscape, with his successors continuing to navigate the complexities of statecraft and diplomacy.

The ūl P'aso's influence can be seen in the many temples and monuments built throughout Goguryeo, which serve as testaments to his enduring legacy. One notable example is the Yongwangsa Temple, dedicated to the worship of King Gogukcheon, whose reign was marked by significant military campaigns led by Ŭl P'aso.
